A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReScene4D and include the main paper and Appendices A–E. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite appendix reflow and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original 3RScan segmentation experiments, baseline comparisons and component ablations in Tables 1–8, alongside qualitative predictions.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds temporal feature-similarity measurements, longer-sequence evaluations and matched-training comparisons in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The joint-query architecture, backbones, contrastive loss, temporal masking and decoder serialization are unchanged. Explicitly describing registered inputs clarifies the existing setup: v1 already used registered scans.

E1.justification: The datasets and indoor segmentation tasks remain unchanged. Appendix C.2 and Figure 8 extend evaluation to three- and four-stage sequences, testing identity maintenance beyond v1's paired-scan setting.

E2.justification: Existing comparisons retain Mask4D, Mask4Former and Mask3D with semantic or geometric matching. The added training controls and sequence-length experiment reuse these comparators; no comparison method is introduced or replaced.

E3.justification: v2 adds the t-sim diagnostic and inference-only evaluation over sequence lengths T=1–4. Appendix C.3 also adds ReScene4D(M) controls using ScanNet pretraining followed by 3RScan training, and 3RScan-only training from scratch. The original experimental settings remain.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, v2 adds direct feature-consistency analysis, longer-sequence robustness testing and controls for training-data/pretraining advantages. These substantively broaden the evidence addressing the proposed mechanism, identity drift and baseline-comparison fairness.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new t-sim averages and sequence-length curves do not introduce uncertainty estimation or error bars.

E6.justification: Existing table scores are retained. New results include Concerto t-sim of 0.8640 without sharing and 0.9198 with contrastive loss plus serialization, and declining temporal AP with longer sequences. Appendix C.3 reports matched-training margins of +14.9 over Mask4Former and +19.0 over Mask4D, without explicitly identifying their metric.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 introduces t-sim, defined as average cosine similarity of an instance's features across paired temporal stages. The existing task definition, loss equations, t-IoU/t-mAP definitions and ambiguous-instance assignment algorithm remain unchanged; no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The introduction qualifies v1's broad avoidance of geometric-overlay assumptions as avoiding forced identity equality for geometrically aligned points. The central task, temporal-fusion contributions and state-of-the-art claim are retained.

C2.justification: v2 explains that feature consistency does not guarantee segmentation quality, discusses identity drift on longer sequences, and identifies unregistered-scan training as future work. Section 3.3 also explicitly states that temporal masking has no effect without voxel overlap.

D1.justification: v2 adds project/supplementary-video access information and discloses that the dataset mixture ratio was selected through preliminary Minkowski experiments. Existing hardware, training-budget and hyperparameter details remain; public release of the metric implementation is still prospective.

R1.justification: Section 2 narrows the novelty distinction to jointly integrating and refining information across observations. Section 4 revises the critique of LSTQ toward identity switches and small indoor instances. The cited-work set is unchanged; publication-detail updates do not add research coverage.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify the abstract, geometric assumptions, metric motivation and baseline rationale. A longer-sequence subsection is inserted into Appendix C, with associated renumbering and minor language/bibliography corrections; the overall organization is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel sequence-length Figure 8 and t-sim columns to Tables 6–8. Table 5 and Figure 7 move, subsequent figures are renumbered, and a malformed caption is corrected. Existing figure images are retained.

improvement.justification: The added training controls address comparison fairness, while feature diagnostics and longer-sequence testing clarify temporal behavior and limitations. More precise registration wording also improves clarity. These are useful but bounded gains: the longer-sequence study is preliminary, and the new matched-training comparisons report only prose margins without explicitly naming the metric.
